3. Leave was granted to consider the following points: (i) the rule of practice relating to 60 days limitation for filing revisional application in criminal case not being an inflexible rule, whether the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division was justified in dismissing the revisional application merely on ground of delay without considering the merit of the case. 

 4. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant submitted that limitation for filing Criminal revision in the High Court Division being not inflexible the learned Judge of the High Court Division in the facts and circumstances of the case erred in not condoning the delay on the cognent reasons shown by the appellant and to consider the case on merit in view of the fact that the ingredients of offence under section 405 of the Penal Code i.e. criminal breach of trust have neither been alleged by the complainant in the petition of complaint nor the same have been proved during trial and as such the appellant's conviction under section 406 of the Penal Code has caused serious miscarriage of justice. Mr. Islam further submits that the money alleged to have been received by the appellant from the complainant as loan upon execution of a hand note became the money of the appellant as soon as it was delivered to him and as such there cannot be any question of entrustment with the said money so far as the appellant is concerned and the use of such money by the appellant does not constitute any offence of criminal breach of trust as has been defined in section 405 of the Penal Code. 

 There is no prescribed period of limitation either in the Code of Criminal Procedure or in the Limitation Act, 1908 for revision. As a matter of long standing practice in the High Court Division 60 days limitation, provided under Article 155 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act for appeal, is being followed for revision. But there is no legal bar to entertain in the interest of justice such revisional application even after the aforesaid period of 60 days provided the applicant can show that he was prevented by sufficient cause to move the High Court Division within the said period of 60 days. Moreover in the absence of any limitation prescribed for revision under the law, it cannot also. be properly said that the application filed beyond 60 days is barred by limitation. The revisional court is to look into the question whether there has been gross negligence on the part of the petitioner or an inordinate delay in moving such revisional application. The appellant's revisional application was filed on the 28th day after the expiry of the said period of 60 days. The learned Judge did not accept the contention of the appellant that being an old man of 72 he had been suffering for the last 2 months before moving the High Court Division and that he also could not arrange for any tadbirkar for the case. It appears that along with the revisional application a separate application under section 5 of the Limitation Act was filed, for condonation of delay. The learned Judge was not satisfied with the reasonings shown by the appellant for the delay of 28 days. 

 7. In the exercise of judicial discretion to dispose of the appellant's revisional application the learned Judge of the High Court Division did not consider the nature of allegations made against him in the petition of complaint and the findings arrived at the courts below in convicting him under section 406 of the Penal Code. On the face of the judgment of the courts below it is clear that both the trial court as well as the appellate Court failed to consider as to whether a loanee for the loan amount can be charged for criminal breach of trust at the instance of the loaner. On behalf of the appellant it was clearly brought to the notice of the High Court Division that refusal for non-payment of loan does not constitute the offence of criminal breach of trust. The learned Judge of the High Court Division did not take into consideration that aspect of the case and rejected the revisional application summarily on the ground of limitation only. Under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal procedure, the High Court Division may also suo motu call for the record of the courts subordinate to it and set aside any order passed by such courts in any legal proceeding which has caused miscarriage of justice.
